summary: A 24-minute manager 1-1 between Chris Klevan and Richard Claessen. Most of it is a post-mortem on a prospect called Jason who was effectively bought in, asked about financing, then rescheduled twice with a crying child and a work issue and finally went dark. Chris's coaching is that Richard chased the sale rather than the person, and should lead a re-engagement with 'is everything okay?' rather than a question about the missed booking. That opens into a longer piece on operating from love and truth rather than niceness. The back half is operational: follow-up cadence and hot/warm/cold pipeline lists in Close, using client result screenshots in follow-up, the reassignment of the departed rep Ben's old leads to Richard, and where the business is going on marketing — a new VSL, a new ad campaign, and cold traffic that will need a different close than the current organic leads. Ends with Chris agreeing to review Richard's worst call of the day.
notable: Richard reports having closed a prospect on a monthly payment outside the two published tiers: 'with the other guy, I eventually closed him like a $200 per month payment'. He describes that same call as 'just so terrible' and says the prospect lacked urgency — 'he was like, yeah, I want it, but not really the urgency there'.

An automated bot answers inbound prospect messages in the same thread the rep then writes in, with nothing marking the handover: 'he said, like, is the paper credit available right after the meeting? Then the bot replied, send me my email address, et cetera. Then I actually sent him a message on the, through that same chat.'

Chris's stated follow-up cadence for non-responders: 'Until they tell me no. Until they tell me to stop' — daily while an answer is outstanding, then weekly, with hot (closes within two weeks), warm (30-60 days) and cold (90+ days) lists maintained in Close.

Chris coaches a concern-first re-engagement message and predicts the response it will produce: 'by you being different and saying, like, hey, putting all this aside for a second, are you okay?... because you're like going to extremes of like showing real concern, they're probably gonna respond.' He frames it explicitly against selling — 'you're showing genuine care about the person versus like genuine care about still the sale happening'.
Chris states a personnel standard: 'I don't keep closers on the team that don't say the thing they need to say, because you're not operating from truth.'
Richard self-describes as 'maybe I'm too nice of a closer now, and I just give them too much room to just get away', and names people-pleasing as the block.

The departed rep Ben Byrne's leads have been handed to Richard and include long-untouched records: 'you've given me the leads from Ben as well... Quite old ones already that just haven't been messaged'.

Marketing state of play: lead flow is currently all organic and volatile, ads have just started, a new VSL and full campaign are weeks out, and Trevor is being asked to post client results because 'right now, when you look at his page, you don't really see much about clients, like, at all'. His bio claims he has worked with 1,200 people.

Chris flags that cold traffic will require a different call than the current warm organic leads: 'most of these guys are going to come in already knowing Trevor... cold traffic is going be more like, I like the idea of kettlebells, but I have no idea who Trevor is.'

Richard names the two calls he has left that day, one of which is the Tyler Kirkwood call recorded the same afternoon: 'Tyler, very, like, I know we can help him... he wants to lose 10% body fat', followed by 'So yeah, I'm going to close one of them at least.'

Richard recounts a think-about-it objection from a prospect who was himself a salesman and says he mishandled it: 'I was like, okay, when you were talking to other people, do you just let them go? And I should have done it differently... So yeah, I screwed up there at the end.'
Recording disclosure was made at the top of the call: 'This meeting is being recorded.'
